items.definition:
a person who informs on a person or organization engaged in an illicit activity
The whistleblower exposed the company's illegal practices.

an award or privilege granted as a special honor or as an acknowledgment of merit
She received many accolades for her groundbreaking research.

strong hostility
There was a deep animosity between the rival teams.

a small rented farm, especially in Scotland
The old man lived in a small croft by the sea.

the removal of regulations or controls
The government announced plans for further deregulation of the industry.

the reduction or withdrawal of military forces and weapons
The treaty called for complete nuclear disarmament.

the process or state of diverging
There was a clear divergence of opinion between the two parties.

the state of being equal in value, amount, function, meaning, etc.
The two systems achieved equivalence in terms of performance.

the painless killing of a patient suffering from an incurable and painful disease or in an irreversible coma
The debate around euthanasia raises complex ethical questions.

a tendency to do nothing or to remain unchanged; a property of matter
The company's inertia prevented it from adapting to new market trends.

a violent uprising against an authority or government
The government quickly suppressed the insurrection.

the act of severely damaging or disfiguring something
The ancient artifact showed signs of deliberate mutilation.

a rare metallic element; a safeguard
Palladium is a valuable metal used in catalytic converters.

a district under the government of a prefect
Kyoto Prefecture is a popular tourist destination in Japan.

a feeling of intense pleasure or joy
She listened to the music with an expression of pure rapture.

a cloth used to wrap a dead body; something that conceals
A thick mist acted as a shroud, obscuring the mountain peaks.

the act of asking for or trying to obtain something
The charity's fundraising campaign involved a direct mail solicitation.

a magical or ethereal quality; cosmic dust
The old theater seemed to be sprinkled with stardust and memories.

a prolonged bitter quarrel or campaign against someone
The family feud escalated into a full-blown vendetta.

a municipal officer
The alderman presented the new city budget.

the state of being isolated from a group or activity
Social alienation can lead to feelings of loneliness.

an eating disorder
Anorexia is a serious condition that requires medical attention.

a drug used to treat depression
The doctor prescribed an antidepressant to help with her mood.

the process of reducing something's strength or effectiveness through sustained attack or pressure
The company is trying to reduce employee attrition.

heavy material used to improve stability
The ship needed more ballast to remain stable in the storm.

the action or process of changing in shape or distorting
The earthquake caused significant deformation of the land.

a machine that generates electricity; an energetic person
She's a real dynamo, always full of energy and new ideas.

a magical or medicinal potion
The old alchemist sought the elixir of life.

a moment of sudden and great revelation or realization
He had an epiphany about his career path during his vacation.

a person who adheres strictly to a set of beliefs, especially religious ones
The fundamentalist group held a strict interpretation of their sacred texts.

intense dislike or disgust
She felt a deep loathing for injustice.

the death or suffering of a martyr
The story of his martyrdom inspired many.

death (often in 'post-mortem')
The post-mortem examination revealed the cause of death.

a creative work, especially a musical composition
Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is considered a masterpiece, his greatest opus.

the official proving of a will
The family had to go through probate to settle the estate.

a natural tendency or inclination
He has a propensity for getting into trouble.

trick; stratagem
It was all a ruse to get him out of the house.

a method of rapid writing
She took notes in shorthand during the meeting.

the state of being unique or individual; a point at which spacetime becomes infinite
The black hole's singularity is a point of infinite density.

the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet
In mathematics, theta is often used to represent an angle.

a sensation of whirling and loss of balance
She suffered from vertigo whenever she looked down from a high place.

a British nobleman ranking above a baron and below an earl
The viscount inherited the family estate after his father's passing.

a salt or ester of acetic acid
The film was made of cellulose acetate.

the quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating
The city's allure was undeniable, drawing in tourists from all over the world.

a serious bacterial disease of sheep and cattle, transmissible to humans
Scientists are studying a vaccine for anthrax.

hostility to or prejudice against Jewish people
The organization works to combat antisemitism and promote tolerance.

a type of cancer that starts in cells that make up the skin or the tissue lining organs
The biopsy revealed a basal cell carcinoma.

the action of looking thoughtfully at something for a long time; deep reflective thought
He spent hours in quiet contemplation of the painting.

national treasury (especially in the UK)
The Chancellor of the Exchequer announced new tax policies.

courage in pain or adversity
She showed great fortitude during her illness.

a badge or distinguishing mark
The general wore his military insignia proudly.

the way in which two or more things affect each other
The interplay between light and shadow created a dramatic effect.

natural juice or gravy
The chef served the roast beef with a rich jus.

one's family and relations; people with similar beliefs
She felt a strong connection with her kindred spirits.

a large group or mass (often used in "en masse")
The employees resigned en masse after the announcement.

a detailed written study of a single specialized subject or an aspect of it
She published a monograph on ancient Roman pottery.

a volume containing several novels or other items previously published separately
The publisher released an omnibus edition of the author's early works.

the study of drugs and their effects
She is studying pharmacology at university.

the place of origin or earliest known history of something
The painting's provenance was carefully documented.

a senior administrative officer in a university or college
The university provost announced new academic policies.

remedy or compensation for a wrong or grievance
The company offered financial redress to the affected customers.

the rebirth of a soul in a new body
Many religions believe in the concept of reincarnation.

Fragments of a bomb, shell, or other object thrown out by an explosion
The explosion sent shrapnel flying in all directions.

A single person or thing
In bridge, a singleton is a suit with only one card.
